step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Identify all architecture components visual in the whiteboard diagram and described in the audio transcript:
   - Mobile Device (UserConsumerMobile): Customer mobile interface used to view usage, access web portal, or display barcodes.
   - ELB (ELB): Elastic Load Balancer routing web traffic from mobile devices to the app tier.
   - Retailer (R) (ThirdParty): Retail partners like Walgreens or CVS where barcodes are scanned for cash payments.
   - EC2 App Server (EC2): Compute instance executing business rules and payment logic.
   - Utility Company (UTIL) (ThirdParty): Utility company system receiving processed payment notifications.
   - Meter (M) (ThirdParty): Physical home utility meter controlled by the utility company.
   - Database (RDS/SQL Server) & EC2 DB Host (EC2): Windows EC2 instance hosting SQL Server in a multi-AZ HA setup.
   - S3 (S3): Object storage receiving database backups with cross-region replication for DR.

2. Trace and define logical flows:
   - Flow 0 (Web Payment): Mobile Device -> ELB -> EC2 App Server -> Utility Company -> Meter.
   - Flow 1 (Retail Checkout Payment): Mobile Device -> Retailer -> EC2 App Server.
   - Flow 2 (Database Backup & Disaster Recovery): Database -> EC2 DB Host -> S3.

graph.categories: Prepaid Utilities, Payment Processing, Disaster Recovery
graph.notes: PAYGO architecture on AWS enabling real-time utility usage tracking, payment processing via web or retail checkout, and high availability/disaster recovery using EC2 multi-AZ stacks and S3 cross-region replication.

nodes.name: Mobile Device
nodes.notes: Customer smartphone or web device used to view utility usage and present checkout barcodes.

nodes.name: ELB
nodes.notes: Load balancer entry point for utility web portals.

nodes.name: Retailer (R)
nodes.notes: Participating retail store (e.g. Walgreens, CVS) where customers pay using printed or mobile barcodes.

nodes.name: EC2 App Server
nodes.notes: EC2 app tier evaluating payment rules, customer validation, and routing payment data.

nodes.name: Utility Company (UTIL)
nodes.notes: Utility system that receives payment confirmation and sends signals to customer meters.

nodes.name: Meter (M)
nodes.notes: Physical utility meter on customer home, turning on within ~25 seconds of payment received.

nodes.name: Database
nodes.notes: SQL Server database running on Windows OS within EC2.

nodes.name: EC2 DB Host
nodes.notes: Host compute instance running SQL Server in a multi-AZ HA architecture.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: S3 bucket storing database backups, replicated across regions for disaster recovery.

edges.notes: Customer accesses utility website via smartphone
ELB routes web traffic to EC2 application server
EC2 app server transmits payment details to utility company
Utility company communicates with customer home meter to restore power
Customer presents barcode on mobile device at participating retailer
Retailer scans barcode and sends transaction to EC2 app server for business rule checks
SQL Server database runs hosted on Windows EC2 host instance
EC2 database host backs up data to S3 for cross-region replication
